page: Microsoft Azure D32ps_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the 64-bit ARM architecture. It is powered by an Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz, featuring 32 dedicated physical cores with one thread per core for a total of 32 vCPUs. The hardware configuration includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with hardware-accelerated AES cryptography support. The virtual machine is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes no bundled local storage and no GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage architectures.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent multi-threaded throughput across general compute tasks, scoring 57,217.14 in stress-ng multi-core and 12,952.0 in Geekbench multi-core. Memory bandwidth tests yield 170.09 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 77.1 GB/sec for writes. The server sustains 41.25 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and 32.88 GB/sec in static web serving. Conversely, single-threaded metrics show limitations typical of the Neoverse-N1 core, reflected in a Geekbench single-core score of 1,104.0 and reduced throughput on bzip3 decompression and text processing. Large-scale language model inference on 70B parameter models falls within the lower performance tiers due to the lack of hardware acceleration and specialized matrix instruction sets.

The D32ps_v5 offers favorable resource density and predictable performance by dedicating full physical cores without simultaneous multithreading overhead. Because the instance contains no ephemeral disk, workloads must be architected around network-attached premium storage. The platform is best suited for scale-out Linux application tiers, microservice orchestration, CI/CD compilation jobs, multi-threaded database operations, and high-concurrency web serving.
description: Microsoft Azure D32ps_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the 64-bit ARM architecture. Powered by a 3.0 GHz Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor, the instance provides 32 dedicated physical cores with a 1:1 thread-to-core mapping and 128.0 GB of memory, equating to 4.0 GB per core. The server includes no local disk storage or GPU accelerators, operating entirely with remote attached storage. Benchmark testing highlights reliable multi-core processing, sustained memory throughput, and steady results across Redis caching, static web hosting, and software compilation. However, single-threaded processing and large-scale AI inference exhibit lower throughput due to architecture and feature set constraints. By avoiding hyperthreading contention across its 32 physical cores, the D32ps_v5 delivers cost-efficient resource utilization for multi-threaded enterprise workloads, web services, container platforms, and distributed database systems.
